_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 To-Do button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule-8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff (this file is the handoff distilled for the dashboard). Check-off state lives in each viewer's browser (localStorage) and resets when _as_of changes. Keep it SHORT — ≤ ~12 items; done items are deleted, not checked.
_as_of: 2026-08-08 · SkyNaut — your Access table is in Supabase and verified, and we now know what share of CPL credit actually reaches a real course: 60%.
_status: Your student data is loaded — 220,588 rows, 42,346 students, 111 colleges — and it checks out exactly against your Access count. Out of it comes a number the CPL Initiative has never had: of all the credit colleges have actually awarded, 60% goes to a real course, 32% to a general-education area (nearly always CSU-GE Area E) and 8% to a generic elective. Put differently, 47% of every CPL student in the system — 20,098 people — has at least one award pointed at Area E, which is exactly what the Veteran Sprint is trying to move away from. And 71% of all recommendations have had nothing awarded at all. Two caveats worth holding onto: these are counts of recommendations, not credits — the credit totals need your second Access table — and the per-college version is deliberately not built yet, because publishing small per-college numbers safely needs the suppression rules we ratified today.

items.text: 📤 EXPORT THE SECOND TABLE — TblCOLL_STU_EXH_CR_UNIT, the one with the credit amounts. Everything we measured today counts recommendations, not credits, so we still can't answer the big one: how many units of already-earned credit are sitting unawarded. Same procedure as today and it'll go faster now that we've done it once. ⚠️ One thing to expect: Supabase's importer quietly duplicated about 2,000 rows on the first load and still said it succeeded. We caught it by comparing counts. We'll do the same check again — don't trust the success message on its own.

❓ WHY 111 COLLEGES AND NOT 123? — twelve of MAP's colleges have no rows at all in the export. That's either genuinely no CPL activity, or a filter somewhere in how the data was pulled. Worth knowing before we publish anything per-college, because a college that's missing looks identical to a college at zero, and those need very different conversations.

📞 ASK MALONE FOR TWO THINGS — (1) the published name of the student-detail view; it still isn't live (the API says 'not Valid'), and once it is, this whole Access export retires and becomes a daily refresh. (2) A stable per-student ID in it, ideally scrambled on their side — without one we can only count recommendations, not people.

📬 SIX FEEDBACK REPORTS STILL NEED YOU — the inbox is clean (our test robot's rows are filtered out of both the queue and the counts). The most useful: someone asked how many colleges have a CPL counsellor listed and Sierra couldn't answer, though she names them one at a time — that's a build, not a bug, and the data already exists. The rest need an eye: Modesto showing 75 early-childhood recommendations against 4 on its landing page; Sierra reading the Fullerton catalogue in one answer and not the next. ⚠ Please don't invite the MAP and CO teams until this has an owner — it's CA-06 on the ⚖️ Governance tab.

🔗 STILL UNCHECKED: THE LINK SIERRA GIVES STUDENTS — creditforbeingyou.org/main/student. I can't reach that domain from here, so it has never been confirmed and it's now in front of every student who asks. One click tells us; it's a one-line fix if it's wrong.

⚖️ FOUR GOVERNANCE ROWS NEED AN OWNER — DR-11 (who decides what Sierra tells the public — so far that's been you personally), CA-06 (Sierra feedback triage, which shows its own untriaged count live), OQ-07 (what must be true before inviting the MAP and CO teams) and OQ-08 (how new surfaces get onto the register at all).

⚠️ HEADS-UP, NOT A BUG YOU NEED TO REPORT — 'Clear owner' does nothing on three cadences (the daily dashboard, the users sync, and the checkpoint loop), because those carry an owner in the register file itself rather than an assigned one. It'll look exactly like the two-click save bug coming back. It isn't, it's written up, and it's on the list.

📊 BUILD THE PER-COLLEGE VERSION — the statewide 60/32/8 split is the headline; the per-college split is what a coordinator can act on. ⚠ This is the one that needs care: cells get thin fast, so it follows the rules ratified today — hide anything under 10 students, hide a second cell alongside it (otherwise the hidden one is recoverable by subtraction), and never rank colleges publicly. Frame it as unclaimed opportunity, never a grade.

🔧 GIVE SIERRA THE 'WHAT HAPPENED' NUMBERS — she can say what credit exists but never what a college has acted on. The data is now in Supabase, so this is a join plus a safely-suppressed summary. ⚠ It touches the shared table behind the widget on colleges' own pages — walk Sam through what changes and who sees it before touching it.

🔍 FINISH THE POACHING AUDIT — four sessions running now. Re-run the five-part review (Sierra's rule text, her per-audience voices, the context builders, the live guidance rows in the 🧭 pane, and the sibling report generators) to confirm nothing still tells her to stay quiet about a fact a student needs.

📚 REFRESH SIERRA'S EXHIBIT LIST — unchanged and still the biggest single limit on her. Her copy covers 2,397 exhibits across 59 colleges; MAP has 123, and her college profiles were last refreshed 25 June. American River, LA Mission and West LA all give CPR credit and she cannot see them. Touches a shared table production reads, so walk Sam through the impact first.

🔬 RE-MEASURE THE 'BIGGEST CHEAPEST WIN' CLAIM — we've been describing basic-training credit as the largest block of unawarded credit in the system. It's true at American River (32 students, every one pointed at Area E, none awarded) and false at Allan Hancock (all of it applied, to real courses). ⭐ The variance between colleges is probably the better story — 'some colleges have solved this, here's what solved looks like' lands better than 'colleges haven't done this.'
